summary: The agent used hyperpowers:brainstorming but called the task "bounded". It gave a short design in chat and wrote no spec document, so it never escalated to the architectural path. It asked one scoping question, got approval, then edited app.js.
reasoning: Criterion 1 passes: the brainstorming skill was loaded before any code changed. Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail. The agent said "Classification: **bounded** ... short design in chat, no spec file". No docs/ directory or specs file exists, and it implemented straight from the in-chat design. Criterion 5 passes because it did not treat the task as a spike. Because the classification escalation is the main thing this scenario checks, the overall result is a fail.

observations.description: The router picked bounded even though the agent's own first message said "adding a parameter changes a signature that callers depend on, so it needs a design agreed". It spotted the public-interface concern and still skipped the spec path.

The design itself was thoughtful. It suggested returning userId from login() instead of adding a parameter, which avoided changing the signature. That may be why it felt bounded, but it quietly changed the public return shape of login(), and the brief also hinted at cross-app tracking. It never asked whether tracking needs to persist or be used by other forms.

The first-run onboarding asked four things in a row: theme picker, security notes, folder trust, and the bypass-permissions warning. In both the trust and bypass prompts the pre-selected choice is 'No, exit', so just pressing Enter would quit the launcher.
After some dialogs the screen stayed blank for several seconds before the next one showed, so it looked frozen for a moment.
The agent planned to put a made-up placeholder userId (user-${username}) in code. It labelled it stub-only and offered null as an alternative, which was reasonable.

criteria.evidence: Session log: the first assistant tool_use was {"tool":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming",...}}. The Edit calls on app.js came after it.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before approval
criteria.evidence: Session log text: "Classification: **bounded** — `login()` and its one caller both already exist in `app.js`, so this is a short design in chat, no spec file." Running `ls -R coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory", and `find ... -path '*specs*'` returned nothing.

criteria.criterion: Spec document presented for review before implementation
criteria.evidence: No spec document was written. The only approval gate was an in-chat design ending "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." After I said "looks good, go ahead" it replied "Approved — implementing." and edited app.js.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: It said "Classification: **bounded** ... short design in chat, no spec file" and then worked from the in-chat design. git status shows only ' M app.js', with no spec file committed or created.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The log's only classification statement is "bounded". No probe plan or spike wording appeared on screen or in the log.
